I'm not an expert, and no doubt others have answered your questions more succinctly than I, but you did reply so I'll give you what I've got, with the analogy of an office.

CPU: The person working in the office. Every time you do something on a computer, like calculate 1+1, it's sent to the CPU to figure out, and it's measured in Hz (cycles per second), 3Ghz is about 3,000,000,000 cycles per second. Dual core: the work is shared between 2 people; quadcore, the work is shared between 4 people.

Overclocking: making the CPU work harder/faster. The faster you go, the more heat is generated, that needs to be cooled down with a fan or liquid cooling. Too hot, your CPU breaks: workers quit.

RAM (random access memory): How much desk space / whiteboard space the person/people working in the office get to use. More ram means they can have more files/programs open at once, and can switch between the two easily.

HDD: Hard Disk Drive. How much storage space the office has. When the people are finished with a report of calculation, they can either throw the results in the bin (delete them), or they get put into a filing cabinet, storage room, etc. There are two main types: disk, and solid/flash. Hard disk drives are slower, but you can store more shit on them, and they're cheaper. They have moving parts. Solid state drives are faster, but much more expensive. Faster meaning you can take files in or out of the room faster.

Graphics card: draws shit to put on your screen. Very similar to the CPU, but the main job is to draw (render) stuff to put on your screen. When you play a game, each frame is rendered and shown on the screen. The more detail and frames you have, the harder the graphics card needs to work. Very fancy new games are generally very graphics intensive, and require a good graphics card to work properly. This is the board room, where the results are presented to shareholders.

Motherboard: the office where everything takes place. A fancy, expensive office allows for more storage, better workers (CPU), and everything is organised well so that it's only a short walk between the storage room, cubicles, boardroom etc.
